Article.ArticleTitle: Expression of interleukin-27 (IL-27) in the lower airways diseases. Increased levels of IL-27 in early clinical stages of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients.

Abstract.AbstractText: INTRODUCTION Interleukin-27, is a cytokine secreted mostly by antigen presenting cells, key for the Th1 cells immune polarization. Its role in interstitial lung diseases (ILD) as well as in lung cancer has been investigated. OBJECTIVES Assessment of IL-27 expression in the lower airways of patients with selected ILD and early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). PATIENTS AND METHODS IL-27 concentration was examined by ELISA in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) supernatants collected from patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (PS), extrinsic allergic alveolitis (EAA), idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), nonspeciﬁc interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) and I-IIa NSCLC with peripheral localization, as well as in control subjects (n = 14, 30, 12, 14, 16 and 14, respectively). Major BAL lymphocyte subsets were phenotyped, intracellular IL-27 expression in BAL lymphocytes was evaluated by flow cytometry. RESULTS IL-27 concentration in BAL supernatants was significantly increased in Th1-mediated conditions, i.e. in EAA and PS, but not in IPF or NSIP. The highest IL-27 levels, 16.9 (17.5) pg/ml, were detected in NCSLC, as compared to 0.4 (0.2) pg/ml in controls, median (SEM). IL-27 was undetectable in corticosteroid-treated PS patients. Both CD4+ and CD8+ BAL lymphocytes were commonly positive with IL-27, and they are a possible local source of IL-27, since its concentration was positively correlated with total number of BAL lymphocytes, including CD4+ cells. CONCLUSIONS The results support the view on Th1-linked activity of IL-27 in ILD. Early NSCLC clinical stages are characterized by high expression of IL-27 in lower airways. High percentage of BAL CD4+ and CD8+ cells produce IL-27, both in patients and controls.
